definitions.explanation: A place that is far off in distance. Used as a noun referring to a remote location, often in contrast to nearby areas.

examples.japanese: {遠方|えんぽう}のお{客様|きゃくさま}もいらっしゃいます。
examples.english: We also have customers from distant places.

examples.japanese: {遠方|えんぽう}に{住|す}んでいるため、なかなか{会|あ}う{機会|きかい}がない。
examples.english: Since I live far away, I rarely have the chance to meet up.

notes:
A somewhat formal or literary word for a distant place. In everyday speech, {遠|とお}く or {遠|とお}い{所|ところ} is more common, but {遠方|えんぽう} appears frequently in written language, announcements, and polite speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遠方|えんぽう}から — from far away
- {遠方|えんぽう}に{住|す}む — to live far away
- {遠方|えんぽう}のお{客様|きゃくさま} — customers/guests from afar
- {遠方|えんぽう}への{配送|はいそう} — delivery to distant locations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遠|とお}く — far away; more casual and commonly used in daily speech
- {遠隔|えんかく} — remote; used for technology or systems (e.g., {遠隔|えんかく}{操作|そうさ}, remote control)
- {僻地|へきち} — remote/isolated area; carries a nuance of being undeveloped or hard to access
